notes.front: What is the Microsoft Purview portal?
notes.back: The single, unified portal through which you reach the Microsoft Purview solutions, grouped by area.
notes.explanation: Its solutions are organised into four areas: Core, Risk & Compliance, Data Governance and Data Security.
notes.example: Like a shopping centre directory that sorts every shop by floor, but the shops are compliance and data tools.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “The Microsoft Purview portal”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager?
notes.back: A Purview solution that helps you assess and manage compliance automatically across a multicloud environment.
notes.explanation: It supports each stage of the compliance journey, from spotting data protection risks to reporting to auditors.
notes.example: Like a tax preparation app that turns the rules into a checklist, but for regulations and standards across your cloud services.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “What is Compliance Manager?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is the compliance score in Compliance Manager?
notes.back: A calculation of your overall compliance posture, based on how far you have got with improvement actions.
notes.explanation: Points are awarded for completed actions that help you meet a regulation, standard or policy, and add up to the score.
notes.example: Like a fitness tracker’s daily score from completed activities, but the activities are compliance tasks.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Compliance score”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Compliance Manager, what is a control?
notes.back: A requirement of a regulation, standard or policy.
notes.explanation: It defines how to assess and manage the system settings, organisational process and people needed to meet that requirement.
notes.example: Like one clause in a building code, such as “fire doors must close on their own”, together with how an inspector checks it.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Controls”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Compliance Manager, what is an assessment?
notes.back: A grouping of the controls from one particular regulation, standard or policy.
notes.explanation: Completing the actions within it helps you meet the requirements of that standard, regulation or law.
notes.example: Like an exam paper built from one syllabus, but each question is a control you must satisfy.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Assessments”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Compliance Manager, what does the Regulations page show?
notes.back: The regulations and certifications for which Compliance Manager offers control-mapping templates.
notes.explanation: Each regulation there is a template you can turn into an assessment.
notes.example: Like a library catalogue of rulebooks, where borrowing one gives you a ready-made checklist.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Regulations”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Compliance Manager, what is an improvement action?
notes.back: A recommended step that helps you align with data protection regulations and standards.
notes.explanation: Improvement actions gather compliance work in one place, and completing them earns points towards the compliance score.
notes.example: Like a ticket in a to-do app that says what to change, who owns it and how far it has got.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Improvement actions”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which area of the Microsoft Purview portal holds foundational capabilities such as Audit, Data Map, Settings and Workflows?
notes.back: Core.
notes.explanation: These are shared building blocks rather than solutions for one risk.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “The Microsoft Purview portal”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which area of the Microsoft Purview portal groups solutions for managing critical risks and regulatory requirements, such as Communication Compliance and Information Barriers?
notes.back: Risk & Compliance.
notes.explanation: Compliance Manager, eDiscovery and Records Management sit in the same area.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “The Microsoft Purview portal”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which area of the Microsoft Purview portal holds tools for governing data across your data estate, such as Data Catalog and Data Policy?
notes.back: Data Governance.
notes.explanation: Data Lifecycle Management is listed in this area too.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “The Microsoft Purview portal”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which area of the Microsoft Purview portal holds tools for protecting sensitive information, such as Information Protection?
notes.back: Data Security.
notes.explanation: Data Loss Prevention and Insider Risk Management are listed in this area too.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “The Microsoft Purview portal”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Under which set of solutions in the Microsoft Purview portal does Compliance Manager sit?
notes.back: Risk & Compliance.
notes.explanation: It sits alongside the other solutions for managing risks and regulatory requirements.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “What is Compliance Manager?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Does Compliance Manager track compliance only for Microsoft 365?
notes.back: No. It also covers resources in other cloud environments, across a multicloud estate.
notes.explanation: Microsoft describes it as assessing and managing compliance across your multicloud environment, not just Microsoft 365.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “What is Compliance Manager?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which stages of the compliance journey does Compliance Manager help with? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: identifying data protection risks, implementing controls, keeping up with regulations and certifications, reporting to auditors.
notes.explanation: Microsoft says it supports the journey at every stage, and lists these four.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “What is Compliance Manager?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Compliance Manager feature gives you ready-made evaluations based on common regional and industry regulations and standards?
notes.back: Prebuilt assessments; admins can also create custom ones for needs unique to the organisation.
notes.explanation: Assessments are the first item in Microsoft’s list of what Compliance Manager provides.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “What is Compliance Manager?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Compliance Manager feature helps admins complete the organisation’s risk assessments efficiently?
notes.back: Its workflow capabilities.
notes.explanation: Microsoft lists workflow capabilities among the four things Compliance Manager provides to simplify compliance.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “What is Compliance Manager?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Compliance Manager feature gives admins step-by-step things to do to meet the regulations and standards that matter to them?
notes.back: Improvement actions.
notes.explanation: Some of these actions Microsoft manages for you, and admins see implementation details and audit results for them.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “What is Compliance Manager?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does Compliance Manager award points for?
notes.back: Completing improvement actions that help you comply with a regulation, standard or policy.
notes.explanation: Those points combine into the overall compliance score.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Compliance score”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In the compliance score, what are “your points”?
notes.back: Points for improvement actions your organisation completes, reflecting controls it is responsible for.
notes.explanation: They are one of the two kinds of points in the score.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Compliance score”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In the compliance score, what are Microsoft-managed points?
notes.back: Points for actions Microsoft has already completed for you as the cloud service provider.
notes.explanation: They count towards your score even though your organisation did not do the work.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Compliance score”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: When you first use Compliance Manager, your initial compliance score is based on the Microsoft 365 {{c1::data protection baseline}}.
notes.back: data protection baseline
notes.explanation: You start from a baseline score rather than from nothing.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Compliance score”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does the Microsoft 365 data protection baseline cover?
notes.back: Key regulations and standards for data protection and general data governance.
notes.explanation: The Compliance Manager documentation describes it as a set of controls.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager, “Understanding your compliance score”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Do all improvement actions add the same number of points to the compliance score?
notes.back: No. Each action’s point value differs, depending on the potential risks involved.
notes.explanation: That difference is what lets the score help you decide which action to focus on first.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager, “Understanding your compliance score”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does a higher compliance score tell you at a glance?
notes.back: That more improvement actions have been completed.
notes.explanation: Understanding your compliance posture at a glance is the first use Microsoft lists for the score.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Compliance score”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does the compliance score help you prioritise compliance work?
notes.back: By pointing you to the improvement actions with the highest potential impact on your score.
notes.explanation: Because actions carry different point values, some move the score more than others.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Compliance score”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which use of the compliance score involves watching it change as your organisation implements more controls?
notes.back: Tracking progress over time.
notes.explanation: As more controls are put in place, the score shows the change.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Compliance score”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: To whom does Microsoft suggest reporting compliance status using the compliance score? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: leadership, auditors, other stakeholders.
notes.explanation: Reporting status is one of the four listed uses of the score.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Compliance score”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which type of Compliance Manager control is Microsoft alone responsible for implementing?
notes.back: Microsoft-managed controls, which are controls for Microsoft cloud services.
notes.explanation: They sit at Microsoft’s end of the split of responsibility.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Controls”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which type of Compliance Manager control is also called customer-managed?
notes.back: Your controls: implemented and managed by your organisation.
notes.explanation: The other two types involve Microsoft, alone or jointly.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Controls”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which type of Compliance Manager control do your organisation and Microsoft both help to implement?
notes.back: Shared controls.
notes.explanation: Responsibility for putting them in place is split between the two.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Controls”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does Compliance Manager keep the status of technical actions up to date?
notes.back: It keeps scanning your Microsoft 365 environment, detects your system settings and updates the status automatically.
notes.explanation: Microsoft calls this continuous assessment of controls.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Controls”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What components make up a Compliance Manager assessment? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: in-scope services, Microsoft-managed controls, your controls, shared controls, an assessment score.
notes.explanation: The assessment score shows progress towards completing the actions needed for compliance.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Assessments”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How can admins create Compliance Manager assessments quickly?
notes.back: From templates, which they can modify to suit their needs.
notes.explanation: All assessments then appear on the Assessments page.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Assessments”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Roughly how many regulatory templates does Compliance Manager provide for creating assessments?
notes.back: Over 360.
notes.explanation: Each template lets you create an assessment quickly for that regulation or certification.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Regulations”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What kind of regulatory template has Compliance Manager added as organisations adopt generative AI?
notes.back: Templates for AI regulations and standards.
notes.explanation: They help assess compliance requirements for AI apps, such as monitoring AI interactions and preventing data loss in them.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Regulations”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What can you do with an improvement action inside your organisation?
notes.back: Assign it to users to carry out the implementation and testing work.
notes.explanation: That is how improvement actions centralise compliance activity.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Improvement actions”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Besides assigning work, what can admins keep within an improvement action? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: documentation, notes, status updates.
notes.explanation: Keeping these with the action keeps its evidence and history in one place.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Improvement actions”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: For improvement actions that Microsoft manages for your organisation, what do admins get?
notes.back: Implementation details and audit results.
notes.explanation: The work is Microsoft’s, but admins can still see how it was done and checked.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “What is Compliance Manager?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does Compliance Manager do with complicated regulations, standards and company policies?
notes.back: Translates them into simple language.
notes.explanation: Microsoft lists this first among Compliance Manager’s benefits.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Benefits of Compliance Manager”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Compliance Manager benefit links regulatory controls to what you should do about them?
notes.back: Mapping regulatory controls against recommended improvement actions.
notes.explanation: Step-by-step guidance on implementing the solutions follows from that mapping.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Benefits of Compliance Manager”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: An admin opens the Microsoft Purview portal to set up Insider Risk Management. In which area will she find it?
notes.back: D: Data Security.
notes.choices:
A) Core
B) Risk & Compliance
C) Data Governance
D) Data Security
notes.choicesExplained: A holds foundational tools such as Audit and Data Map. B holds solutions such as Compliance Manager and eDiscovery. C holds tools such as Data Catalog and Data Lifecycle Management.
notes.explanation: Data Security groups the tools for protecting sensitive information, and Insider Risk Management is listed there.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “The Microsoft Purview portal”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A retailer must show it meets a regional data protection regulation and wants a ready-made starting point in Microsoft Purview. What should it use?
notes.back: A: a prebuilt assessment in Compliance Manager.
notes.choices:
A) A prebuilt assessment in Compliance Manager
B) The Service Trust Portal’s My Library
C) Microsoft Defender for Cloud’s secure score
D) An Azure Policy initiative
notes.choicesExplained: B stores Microsoft’s documents but does not assess your organisation. C and D belong to Azure security and governance, not to Purview’s regulatory assessments.
notes.explanation: Compliance Manager offers prebuilt assessments based on common regional and industry regulations.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “What is Compliance Manager?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Your compliance score rises for an action about physical security in Microsoft’s own datacentres, which nobody in your company worked on. Which kind of points are these?
notes.back: B: Microsoft-managed points.
notes.choices:
A) Your points
B) Microsoft-managed points
C) Baseline points
D) Shared points
notes.choicesExplained: A come from actions your organisation completes. D and C are not kinds of points in the compliance score, which has only your points and Microsoft-managed points.
notes.explanation: Microsoft-managed points come from actions Microsoft has completed on your behalf as the cloud service provider.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Compliance score”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A small compliance team can finish only one of four open improvement actions this month. Using the compliance score, which should it pick?
notes.back: A: the one worth the most points, since it has the highest potential impact.
notes.choices:
A) The one worth the most points
B) The one assigned longest ago
C) Any one: every action is worth the same
D) The one Microsoft manages
notes.choicesExplained: B ignores risk and impact. C is wrong: point values differ with the potential risks involved. D is Microsoft’s work, not the team’s.
notes.explanation: The score helps you prioritise by focusing on actions with the highest potential impact.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Compliance score”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A requirement needs Microsoft to run the underlying service securely and your admins to configure it correctly. Which type of control is this?
notes.back: C: a shared control.
notes.choices:
A) A Microsoft-managed control
B) One of your controls
C) A shared control
D) An assessment
notes.choicesExplained: A is Microsoft’s alone. B is your organisation’s alone. D is a grouping of controls, not a type of control.
notes.explanation: Shared controls are implemented by your organisation and Microsoft together.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Controls”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A bank wants to see, in one place, every control a particular standard requires and how far it has got with them. What should it create in Compliance Manager?
notes.back: B: an assessment for that standard.
notes.choices:
A) A single improvement action
B) An assessment for that standard
C) A new control type
D) A My Library notification
notes.choicesExplained: A is one step, not the whole standard. C: the control types are fixed as Microsoft-managed, yours and shared. D belongs to the Service Trust Portal.
notes.explanation: An assessment groups the controls from one regulation, standard or policy and scores progress on them.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Assessments”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: An admin needs a colleague to test a new setting and attach the test evidence where auditors will find it. Where in Compliance Manager should this work live?
notes.back: D: in the improvement action.
notes.choices:
A) On the Regulations page
B) In the compliance score
C) In the Microsoft Purview portal’s Core area
D) In the improvement action
notes.choicesExplained: A lists regulation templates. B is a calculation, not a place to store work. C holds foundational tools such as Audit, not assigned tasks.
notes.explanation: Improvement actions can be assigned for implementation and testing, and can store documentation and status updates.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Improvement actions”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How do “your points” differ from Microsoft-managed points in the compliance score?
notes.back: Your points come from actions your organisation completes; Microsoft-managed points come from actions Microsoft completed for you.
notes.explanation: The compliance score is made up of these two kinds of points.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Compliance Manager, “Compliance score”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
